rule: Collect publicly bookable Amsterdam-area visitor experiences competing for discovery time/budget; exclude broken/empty/off-area pages.
Minimum 60 valid full-collection listings; working target 80; ceiling 100 unless the research lead documents a coverage reason.
rationale: Prevents arbitrary pursuit of 100 while satisfying the approved range.

rule: Use manual structured public-page review. Automation/scraping is not authorized by this pack.
No single platform should exceed 35% of the analysis-ready listing sample unless access constraints are documented.
rationale: Reduces platform-sampling distortion revealed by the pilot.

rule: Capture the most specific public product-detail URL when available; retain source_url for provenance.
Record an offset-aware observation_datetime for every new full row.
rationale: Prices, ratings and policies are time-sensitive.

rule: Default comparable price scenario is 1 adult standard participant. Document any product-required deviation.
rationale: Creates a consistent price basis without inventing equivalence.

rule: Use one common future service date for each comparison batch. If unavailable, use the documented fallback window and flag the deviation.
Record the exact option/variant used whenever a page offers multiple bookable choices.
rationale: Option differences change price, duration, language and inclusions.

rule: Never overwrite original_price; capture payable displayed value and any visible reference/promotional price separately.
rationale: Maintains raw evidence and permits promo QA.

rule: Classify price as per_person, per_group, bundle, included, not_displayed or unknown before analysis.
Review promotion_flag before any price analysis; crossed-out/reference prices are not treated as payable prices.
Retain display_currency. Normalize only in the analytical layer using one documented FX source/date for the analysis batch.
Blank/NOT_DISPLAYED/unknown must be used according to the dictionary; never convert missing evidence to zero, false, or not offered.
Record only languages explicitly displayed for the observed product/option; NOT_DISPLAYED does not mean monolingual.
Capture public aggregates only; never interpret review count as bookings or demand.
Retain every marketplace listing as an observation. Use product_family_id only after human duplicate review.
Compare operator, product reference, title, duration, itinerary, inclusions, meeting point and options. Title similarity alone cannot authorize a merge.
Every full row must reach CONFIRMED_SAME_FAMILY, CONFIRMED_DISTINCT or documented UNRESOLVED before product-family frequency analysis.
Use one primary category from the dictionary; subcategory can preserve detail. Reclassifications require a transformation note.
Inaccessible or blocked sources are documented as limitations; do not bypass access controls to satisfy quotas.
A second reviewer checks at least 20% of full rows plus every proposed duplicate-family merge and every FX-normalized price rule.
rationale: Adds QA proportionate to judgment risk.

rule: New rows progress RAW → REVIEWED → DUPLICATE_CHECKED → NORMALIZED → ANALYSIS_READY. REJECTED rows remain preserved with reason.
Category shares use validated product families; price statistics use only comparable bases/dates/participant scenarios/currencies after normalization.
rationale: Prevents premature or distorted Article 03 inputs.

rule: Do not open Article 03 until the Article 02 full sample is QA-reviewed, duplicate treatment is documented, price protocol is applied, and the evidence pack is frozen.
